name: cutout_image
description: Cut a person (or any subject) out of a photo or one video frame with BiRefNet (MIT, local GPU; the model downloads on first use, ~450 MB general / ~890 MB portrait) and import the RGBA PNG into the "Cutouts" bin. The edge is cleaned (islands and haze removed, 1 px choke, foreground colour re-estimated under hair, green screens despilled). For the side_cutout sticker look, stroke adds a white outline (strokePx is its thickness when the cut-out is shown 1080 px tall, default 8), shadow a soft drop shadow; the canvas is padded so neither is clipped, and a side the frame edge cuts through stays a straight edge with no stroke. With several people in the frame, pass region around the one you want. Returns assetId (place it with side_cutout or place_clip), bbox of the subject in the source frame (0–1), coverage, and the PNG size. Look at the result before relying on its edge.

assetId.description: Image or video asset to cut from.

clipId.description: A media clip instead of an asset; the frame defaults to the middle of what the clip shows.

path.description: A file on disk that is not imported yet (e.g. a download path).

time.description: Source seconds of the video frame to cut from (default: middle of the clip or asset).

model.description: general (default) for anything; portrait for people with loose hair.

stroke.description: Bake a white sticker outline in (default false).

strokePx.description: Outline thickness when the cut-out is shown 1080 px tall (default 8; 6–10 reads as a sticker).

shadow.description: Bake a soft drop shadow in (default false).

region.description: [x, y, width, height] in frame fractions: only the subject inside is cut out. Use it to pick one person from a group.

choke.description: Pixels to pull the edge in (default 1).

crop.description: Crop to the subject plus room for the stroke and shadow (default true); false keeps the full frame.

name: detect_faces
description: Find and track faces in a video span (or a still) with YuNet (OpenCV Zoo, MIT; CPU, no GPU; 230 KB model fetched on first use). Faces are linked across frames by overlap, so each track is one person. Returns FaceTrack[]: {id, frames:[{t (source seconds), x, y, width, height (0–1 frame fractions), score, mouth:{x, y} (midpoint of the mouth corners)}]} — the path for head_paste and the mouth box for bleep covers. A span defaults to the clip's source range (or 10 s of an asset); at most 3600 frames per call.

clipId.description: A media clip; the span defaults to what the clip shows.

name: key_green_screen
description: Detect a chroma-green backdrop and key it. Samples frames of each clip's source range (FFmpeg + a border/full-frame chroma test, no model), reports greenShare (0–1 share of sampled frames standing on a green backdrop) and the backdrop's colour, and — for every clip whose greenShare is at least minShare — attaches the keylight effect (screen colour, gain and balance solved from the measured backdrop, 50 % spill suppression) exactly as edit_effect would, all in one undo step; an existing keylight on the clip is updated rather than duplicated. Keylight renders in preview and export. Use all: true to scan every video clip of the comp (compId or the active one). After keying, look at a frame for fringe or holes in dark clothes and put something behind the host.

clipId.description: One video clip to check and key.

all.description: Check every enabled video clip of the comp (clips named like a background plate are skipped).

compId.description: Comp for all: true (default: the active comp).

minShare.description: Key a clip when at least this share of its frames is green (default 0.5).

dryRun.description: Measure and report only; attach nothing.
